title: Remaining GCC C++11 gaps after validation batch 5

T.title: Templates: validation, substitution, deduction and identity
T.strategy: Four cooperating subtasks: validate active pack uses at the owning typed boundary; preserve substitution failure and erased-signature obligations; repair deduction/ordering/canonical identity; finish dependent facts before lowering. This is a validation batch, not a claim of one shared code defect.
T.tests: Required PA15/17/18 lanes, refined per source. Pair immediate-context rejection with a successful fallback and an invalid instantiated-body control. Pair singleton and multi-element packs, explicit-prefix extension, empty packs, named/unnamed NTTPs and positive partial-ordering neighbors. Do not instantiate otherwise unused bodies merely to find errors.

D.title: Declaration grammar and class invariants
D.strategy: Separate declaration-purpose checks from class ownership/access checks. Reuse typed declaration kind, owner, access and direct-base facts; validate once when the fact becomes known. Strong subfamilies are union references, inherited constructors and enum access. No global reject predicate.
D.tests: Use each source's earliest owning PA, rather than one late catch-all directory. Pair reference members with legal static/pointer union members, direct and indirect inherited constructors, public/private enumerators, and legal versus illegal attribute/declaration placement. Ordinary malformed declarations remain diagnostic obligations even when a nearby template is unused.

I.title: Initialization, reference binding, overload ranking and lifetime
I.strategy: Keep viability, ranking and selected-candidate validation distinct. Add the missing narrow array/enum/function-reference ranking facts; repair reference-related binding and temporary formation; preserve explicit/deleted/access/destructor obligations. Lifetime cleanup is a separate subtask from forming the conversion.
I.tests: Required PA11/12/15/18 lanes as reduced. Include empty/short/exact lists, differently sized arrays, cv/ref neighbors, copy versus direct list initialization, deleted/private candidate selection, and runtime destruction/lifetime checks. Do not infer correctness from choosing the expected overload alone.

C.title: Constant evaluation, object facts and cast validation
C.strategy: Carry typed storage, lifetime, provenance and known/unknown-value facts. Permit an unknown reference/this until an operation actually reads a value. Validate source category and complete-class requirements before folding a cast. Three positive sources need wording or initializer_list-carrier review before their proposed repair is authorized by the language contract.
C.tests: Primarily required PA16 plus the earliest cast-owning PA. Pair unknown-reference size queries with forbidden value reads, static/lifetime-extended objects with automatic objects, complete and incomplete member-pointer casts, glvalue and prvalue reinterpretation, and valid const_cast class-rvalue neighbors.

E.title: Implicit object, exception specifications and TU linkage
E.strategy: Preserve implicit-object cv and lexical exception context, reuse deferred exception-demand machinery, allow enum range ADL, and validate canonical C linkage and no-linkage-signature definition obligations. These are independent small fixes grouped for validation. One source already has a private prepared fix.
E.tests: Use the earliest PA6/11/15/exception-owning lanes indicated per source. Include mutable/reference members and static/nonconst neighbors, compatible/incompatible friend exception declarations, nested function parameter declarations, enum begin/end ADL, distinct C++ overloads versus C linkage, and same-TU definitions for signatures using local types.

P.title: Declarators, parser disambiguation and literal operator IDs
P.strategy: Five focused parser repairs sharing one validation batch: function-type NTTP adjustment, decltype base mem-initializers, concatenated empty literal-operator strings, trailing-return member pointers and declaration/expression disambiguation. Reuse parsed/typed nodes and bounded existing disambiguation.
P.tests: Required PA7/11/12/14/17 lanes after handout review. Keep named versus unnamed function parameters, ordinary and decltype base names, literal suffix constraints, cv/ref member pointers and declaration/expression neighbors. Never repair parsing by reparsing rendered text.

R.title: Standards, source expectations and IFNDR adjudication
R.strategy: Resolve the exact source and current adopted rule before changing compiler or grading. Keep open/drafting proposals distinct from adopted decisions; NAD can affirm that a program is valid. Fifteen negative TUs need source-specific IFNDR adjudication, not automatic exclusion of every unused template.
R.tests: For each adjudicated source, retain the original observed result and provenance. Add an ordinary or actually instantiated witness and positive neighbors for the meaningful rule. Change a suite expectation only with a recorded language basis; do not count unresolved cases as passes.

X.title: Course, language-mode, vendor-extension and adapter policy
X.strategy: Decide the declared contract for GNU builtins/designators/statement expressions, macro-literal recovery, numeric linemarkers, later attributes, constexpr superset and library carrier layout. Prefer a faithful adapter correction where possible. These are not automatic ISO C++11 implementation defects.
X.tests: Preserve independent core-language obligations when projecting an extension test. Test supported extensions explicitly in their proper course lane. Any applicability or expectation change must be reasoned, versioned and visible, rather than selected according to whether cppgm passes.
